37258-pink-gods-and-blue-demons.title: Pink Gods And Blue Demons
37258-pink-gods-and-blue-demons.creator: Cynthia Stockley
37258-pink-gods-and-blue-demons.description: A book by Cynthia Stockley. Mr Rhodes entertained General French at dinner here after the relief of Kimberley. There is a picture over the dining-room mantelpiece of the two men meeting on the famous occasion of the relief of Kimberley.

38677-the-history-of-antiquity-vol-1-of-.title: Professor Max Duncker,
38677-the-history-of-antiquity-vol-1-of-.creator: Evelyn Abbott, M.A.,
38677-the-history-of-antiquity-vol-1-of-.description: A book by Evelyn Abbott, M.A.,. History knows nothing of her infancy. The beginning of the development of the human race lies beyond the sphere of memory, and so also do the first steps in that development. The early stages of culture--whether in nations or individuals--are unconscious, and unobservant of self; they are therefore without the conditions which make remembrance possible.

arxiv-2005-01149.title: Effective lockdown and role of hospital-based COVID-19 transmission in some Indian states: An outbreak risk analysis Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2005-01149.creator: Tridip Sardar, Sourav Rana
arxiv-2005-01149.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Tridip Sardar, Sourav Rana. There are several reports in India that indicate hospitals and quarantined centers are COVID-19 hotspots. In the absence of efficient contact tracing tools, Govt. and the policymakers may not be paying attention to the risk of hospital-based transmission. To explore more on this important route and its possible impact on lockdown effect, we developed a mechanistic model with hospital-based transmission.

arxiv-2010-01150.title: Cost-effective Selection of Pretraining Data: A Case Study of Pretraining BERT on Social Media
arxiv-2010-01150.creator: Xiang Dai 1,2 Sarvnaz Karimi 1 Ben Hachey 3 Cecile Paris 1 1 CSIRO Data61, Sydney, Australia 2 University of Sydney, Sydney, Australia 3 Harrison ai, Sydney, Australia {dai.dai,sarvnaz.karimi,cecile.paris}@csiro.au ben.hachey@gmail.com
arxiv-2010-01150.description: Abstract Recent studies on domain-specific BERT models show that effectiveness on downstream tasks can be improved when models are pretrained on in-domain data. Often, the pretraining data used in these models are selected based on their subject matter, e.g., biology or computer science.

arxiv-2108-01347.title: Three families of toric rings arising from posets or graphs with small class groups
arxiv-2108-01347.creator: Akihiro Higashitani, Koji Matsushita
arxiv-2108-01347.description: Abstract . The main objects of the present paper are (i) Hibi rings (toric rings arising from order polytopes of posets), (ii) stable set rings (toric rings arising from stable set polytopes of perfect graphs), and (iii) edge rings (toric rings arising from edge polytopes of graphs satisfying the odd cycle condition).

arxiv-2112-07890.title: Investigating myocardial infarction and its effects in patients with urgent medical problems using advanced data mining tools
arxiv-2112-07890.creator: Tanya Aghazadeh, Mostafa Bagheri
arxiv-2112-07890.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tanya Aghazadeh, Mostafa Bagheri. In medical science, it is very important to gather multiple data on different diseases and one of the most important objectives of the data is to investigate the diseases. Myocardial infarction is a serious risk factor in mortality and in previous studies, the main emphasis has been on people with heart disease and measuring the likelihood of myocardial infarction in them through demographic features, echocardiography, and electrocardiogram.

arxiv-2303-08583.title: F-IVM: Analytics over Relational Databases under Updates
arxiv-2303-08583.creator: Ahmet Kara, Milos Nikolic, Dan Olteanu, Haozhe Zhang
arxiv-2303-08583.description: Abstract This article describes F-IVM, a unified approach for maintaining analytics over changing relational data. We exemplify its versatility in four disciplines: processing queries with group-by aggregates and joins; learning linear regression models using the covariance matrix of the input features; building Chow-Liu trees using pairwise mutual information of the input features; and matrix chain multiplication.

arxiv-2307-16889.title: Rethinking Noisy Label Learning in Real-world Annotation Scenarios from the Noise-type Perspective
arxiv-2307-16889.creator: Renyu Zhu, Haoyu Liu, Runze Wu, Minmin Lin, Tangjie Lv, Changjie Fan, Haobo Wang
arxiv-2307-16889.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the problem of learning with noisy labels in real-world annotation scenarios, where noise can be categorized into two types: factual noise and ambiguous noise. To better distinguish these noise types and utilize their semantics, we propose a novel sample selection-based approach for noisy label learning, called Proto-semi.

arxiv-2404-14102.title: Dynamical quantum Ansatz tree approach for the heat equation
arxiv-2404-14102.creator: N. M. Guseynov 1,2 , W. V. Pogosov 1,2,3 , A. V. Lebedev 1,2
arxiv-2404-14102.description: Abstract Quantum computers can be used for the solution of various problems of mathematical physics. In the present paper, we consider a discretized version of the heat equation and address its solution on quantum computer using variational Anzats tree approach (ATA). We extend this method originally proposed for the system of linear equations to tackle full time dependent heat equation.

arxiv-2408-17158.title: Relativistic Exchange Bounds
arxiv-2408-17158.creator: Long Meng, Heinz Siedentop, Matthias Tiefenbeck
arxiv-2408-17158.description: Abstract . We collect estimates of the exchange energy of the relativistic no-pair Hartree-Fock and Müller functional and use them to show the existence of a minimizer and stability of matter of the relativistic Müller functional in the free picture. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 81-V45,35Q40 In admiration on the occasion of Bernard Helffer’s 75th birthday 1.

arxiv-2502-16172.title: Practical programming research of Linear DML model based on the simplest Python code: From the standpoint of novice researchers
arxiv-2502-16172.creator: SHUNXIN YAO
arxiv-2502-16172.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by SHUNXIN YAO. This paper presents linear DML models for causal inference using the simplest Python code on a Jupyter notebook based on an Anaconda platform and compares the performance of different DML models. The results show that current Library API technology is not yet sufficient to enable novice Python users to build qualified and high-quality DML models with the simplest coding approach.

arxiv-2508-07543.title: Towards Automated Commentary Generation for Soccer Highlights
arxiv-2508-07543.creator: Chidaksh Ravuru
arxiv-2508-07543.description: Abstract 1 Abstract Automated soccer commentary generation has evolved from template-based systems to advanced neural architectures, aiming to produce real-time descriptions of sports events. While frameworks like SoccerNet-Caption laid foundational work, their inability to achieve fine-grained alignment between video content and commentary remains a significant challenge.

pmc-10600141.creator: Jorge Espinoza-Derout, Jose Mari Luis Arambulo, William Ramirez-Trillo, Juan Carlos Rivera, Kamrul M Hasan, Candice J Lao, Maria C Jordan, Xuesi M Shao, Kenneth P Roos, Amiya P Sinha-Hikim, Theodore C Friedman
pmc-10600141.description: Electronic cigarettes (e-cigarettes) are a prevalent alternative to conventional nicotine cigarettes among smokers and people who have never smoked. Increased concentrations of serum free fatty acids (FFAs) are crucial in generating lipotoxicity. We studied the effects of acipimox, an antilipolytic drug, on e-cigarette-induced cardiac dysfunction. C57BL/6J wild-type mice on high fat diet were treated with saline, e-cigarette with 2.

pmc-10617123.title: Hypoxia enhances anti-fibrotic properties of extracellular vesicles derived from hiPSCs via the miR302b-3p/TGFβ/SMAD2 axis
pmc-10617123.creator: Milena Paw, Agnieszka A Kusiak, Kinga Nit, Jacek J Litewka, Marcin Piejko, Dawid Wnuk, Michał Sarna, Kinga Fic, Kinga B Stopa, Ruba Hammad, Olga Barczyk-Woznicka, Toni Cathomen, Ewa Zuba-Surma, Zbigniew Madeja, Paweł E Ferdek, Sylwia Bobis-Wozowicz
pmc-10617123.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundCardiac fibrosis is one of the top killers among fibrotic diseases and continues to be a global unaddressed health problem. The lack of effective treatment combined with the considerable socioeconomic burden highlights the urgent need for innovative therapeutic options.

pmc-10626714.title: The effect of lavender aroma for anxiety disorder: a study protocol for a multicenter, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial
pmc-10626714.creator: Haruka Amitani, Ryusei Nishi, Kenichiro Sagiyama, Takamasa Fukumoto, Kouta Funakoshi, Naomi Takayanagi, Hiroko Watanabe, Masayuki Hirose, Koshiro Tagawa, Keiko Ota, Yoichi M Ito, Akihiro Asakawa
pmc-10626714.description: BackgroundAnxiety disorder is the most prevalent psychiatric disorder. Benzodiazepines, which are often used for anxiety in patients with anxiety disorder, have various side effects. Lavender, one of the most commonly used essential oils in aromatherapy, has the potential to reduce benzodiazepine use for anxiety disorders.MethodsThis study is a multicenter, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial.

pmc-11334661.title: Application of the Modified Universal Soil Loss Equation (MUSLE) for the prediction of sediment yield in Agewmariam experimental watershed, Tekeze River basin, Northern Ethiopia
pmc-11334661.creator: Yonas Reda, Awdenegest Moges, Hailu Kendie
pmc-11334661.description: The study utilized the Modified Universal Soil Loss Equation (MUSLE) to predict sediment loss and evaluate the model's performance in the Agewmariam experimental watershed in order to support the planning, management, and appropriate use of the soil and water resources in the watershed. The natural resources conservation service (NRCS) curve number method was used to model runoff energy factor.

pmc-11367856.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of residents towards Hospital-at-Home (HaH) and its role in residency training
pmc-11367856.creator: Rachel Choe, Ian Yi Han Ang, Hooi Swang Cheng, Jonathan E Jacob, Stephanie Qianwen Ko
pmc-11367856.description: BackgroundWith the proliferation of Hospital at Home (HaH) programmes globally, there is a need to equip junior doctors with the skills necessary for provision of HaH care. The ideal training structure and clinical requirements for junior doctors to be considered competent in providing HaH care is still poorly understood.

pmc-11514801.title: Surf therapy for people with mental health disorders: a systematic review of randomized and non-randomized controlled trials
pmc-11514801.creator: Lara Carneiro, Filipe Manuel Clemente, João Gustavo Claudino, José Ferreira, Rodrigo Ramirez-Campillo, José Afonso
pmc-11514801.description: BackgroundSurf therapy is gaining popularity for improving mental health. However, there is limited research evidence to substantiate these claims. Therefore, this systematic review aimed to assess randomized or non-randomized studies analyzing the efficacy of surf therapy in improving symptoms of mental illness compared to non-exercising controls and/or alternative intervention, and to identify evidential gaps to inform future research.

pmc-11520099.title: Type 3 immune response protects against Salmonella Typhimurium infection in the small intestine of neonatal rats
pmc-11520099.creator: Zhipeng Yang, Mei Zhang, Ning Gao, Jian Peng, Hongkui Wei
pmc-11520099.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bacterial infections, particularly Salmonella, pose a significant health risk to neonates due to their underdeveloped immune systems. Understanding the immune responses in the neonatal intestine during S. Typhimurium infection is crucial for developing effective therapeutic and prevention strategies. This study found neonatal rats exhibited severe symptoms, including significant mortality, body weight loss, diarrhea, and bacterial load increases in the gastrointestinal tract and various organs, particularly in the ileum.

pmc-11631496.title: Loss of the Na+/K+ cation pump CATP-1 suppresses nekl-associated molting defects
pmc-11631496.creator: Shaonil Binti, Philip T Edeen, David S Fay
pmc-11631496.description: The conserved Caenorhabditis elegans protein kinases NEKL-2 and NEKL-3 regulate membrane trafficking and are required for larval molting. Through a forward genetic screen, we identified a mutation in catp-1 as a suppressor of molting defects in synthetically lethal nekl-2; nekl-3 double mutants. catp-1 encodes a membrane-associated P4-type ATPase involved in Na+–K+ exchange.

pmc-12542117.title: Pregnancy associated breast cancer: correlation between parity and ultrasonic characteristics of tumors & background echotexture
pmc-12542117.creator: Yue Zhang, Linxiaoxi Ma, Na Hu, Cai Chang, Yi Gao, Yaling Chen
pmc-12542117.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo investigate the characteristics of pregnancy associated breast cancer (PABC) and correlation of parity with ultrasonic tumor and background echotexture, based on the analysis of diagnostic efficiency.MethodsThe ultrasonic images of 184 female patients with PABC and 47 female patients with benign lesions, all of whom were pregnant or within one year postpartum at diagnosis and underwent surgery for their breast conditions in our center from January 2016 to December 2023, were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-12602466.title: Psychological distress, loneliness, and satisfaction with life during the COVID-19 pandemic: a longitudinal study comparing migrants and non-migrants in Norway
pmc-12602466.creator: Pierina Benavente, Lars Thore Fadnes, Gro M. Sandal, Silje Mæland, Stine Lehmann, Esperanza Diaz
pmc-12602466.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately impacted migrants’ health and well-being, with some effects becoming evident months into the crisis. Psychological distress, loneliness, and satisfaction with life, which are indicators closely tied to mental health and well-being, were critically affected during the pandemic. However, comparative longitudinal studies of these parameters across migrant and non-migrant population remain scarce.

pmc-12673826.title: Antiplatelet Therapy Tailored by Ethnicity
pmc-12673826.creator: Joon Ho Ahn, Min Chul Kim
pmc-12673826.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Corresponding Author Over the last several decades, the potent P2Y12 inhibitors ticagrelor and prasugrel have been the treatments of choice instead of clopidogrel for the management of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Recent guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology and the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association recommend ticagrelor over clopidogrel on the basis of the major randomized clinical results of the PLATO (Platelet Inhibition and Patient Outcomes) trial.1,2 However, the efficacy and safety of cardiovascular drugs may vary among ethnicities, with

pmc-13202755.title: Maternal and fetal determinants on kidney size in early childhood: insights from a New York City cohort
pmc-13202755.creator: Rui Ling, Eunsil Seok, Sarai Encarnacion, Vasuda Kapoor, Mengling Liu, Yelena Afanasyeva, Shailee Lala, Fjolla Hyseni Vokshi, Jie Liu, Laura Malaga-Dieguez, Leonardo Trasande
pmc-13202755.description: BackgroundThe role of maternal and fetal characteristics in determining kidney size in early childhood remains largely unexplored. This study aims to evaluate the association between birth weight and kidney size in children aged one to six years and explore other children and maternal determinants in a United States cohort.
